build.summary:
I built physiology-hyperaemia-and-adenosine in the eight listed files plus three new test files. All new tests pass and the typecheck is clean. There is one honest gap: the lab's rig in src/ui/sections/PhysiologyLab.tsx is not in this package's file list. Until it calls the new engine adapter, the chosen dose, line site, caffeine, the adenosine hazards and the bedside orders do not reach the patient engine in the running lab. In the meantime the rig still gives its standard adenosine doses. Two assertions in physiologyTips.test.ts, a test owned by another package, now fail by design; the fix is described under outOfScope.

What changed:
- Patient engine (engine.ts). An adenosine hazard model, off by default and set with setAdenosineHazards. A high-risk intracoronary dose is either above 100 µg into the RCA or a dominant circumflex, or a fast push. Such a dose can bring AV block with no escape rhythm (ventricular standstill), atrial fibrillation (which may revert by itself) or VF after a pause. A preset can force one of these. The model draws from its own random generator, so other labs' results do not change. giveDrug now takes the vessel and the injection speed. New orders: cough(), setPacing(rate), cardiovert() (a synchronised shock), and setRecentCaffeine(). Snapshot and restore carry the new state.
- Drug model (pharmacology.ts). No new drugs. An infusion can carry a delivered fraction (for a tissued line), and caffeine scales down every adenosine effect. Pure closed-form versions of the engine's adenosine model are exported so the session can use them.
- Pressure-wire session (pwSession.ts). Hyperaemia now comes from the engine's adenosine model, so the dose, rate, vein and caffeine all change it. Intracoronary adenosine takes a dose and a speed, and a guide flush delivers the rest of the bolus. IV adenosine takes a rate and a site (hand cannula, large antecubital vein, central vein). Contrast FFR uses 8 mL and the 0.83 cut-off. Failure states: tissued hand line, saline swap, caffeine, low dose, guide disengaged at the bolus, and readings taken before the flush or before the trace recovers from the injection. Readings below hyperaemia 0.9 are flagged submaximal, for the debrief and guided aids only. The session also has the operator's checks (cannula, drug labels, caffeine), bedside orders, a record of arrhythmias from the monitor, and new debrief items. Six presets were added: ic-rca-dose, iv-tissued-line, iv-caffeine, saline-swap, contrast-ffr and adenosine-vf. The engine adapter added here (setUpPwEngine, applyPwActionToEngine, pwPatientInput) is what the rig needs to call. The old dose-free actions keep their curves, so other callers are unchanged.
- Screens. MeasurePanel now offers the dose field (empty), injection speed, guide flush, IV rate and vein, contrast, the three checks, and the monitor's heart rate and mean pressure. It shows OrdersPanel underneath: cough, wait, CPR, pacing, charge, clear, shock, synchronised shock, and a hand-off to the pacing lab's adenosine-block scenario.
- Tips (physiologyTips.ts). Atrial fibrillation and VF are added to raises as PHYSIOLOGY_ADENOSINE_EVENTS, and the adenosine drugs lesson is added to the measure step.
- hyperaemia.launch.ts lists the six presets under pm-physiology-indices and pm-lab-drugs-microvascular.

Snapshots of the five listed files that already existed are in /Users/qc25212/Downloads/Misc/Games and apps/Cath Simulator/datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/physiology-hyperaemia-and-adenosine/, along with the .started marker. OrdersPanel.tsx and hyperaemia.launch.ts were new. I edited only the listed files and added three new test files.

Design decisions to know about:
1. Hyperaemia is the engine's adenosine model, evaluated in closed form from new pure functions in pharmacology.ts, rather than a value sent each tick from the engine. This keeps the reducer engine-free and lets the rig ask for hyperaemia at past times, which its pdAt trace drawing does. Tests check the closed form matches the stepped Pharmacology.
2. Maximal hyperaemia is scaled to the standard doses: IV 140 µg/kg/min at steady state, and IC at the low end of the module's ranges (RCA 50 µg, 14-physiology.ts:410; left 100 µg, 04-lab-drugs.ts:436).
3. The console never refuses a reading because hyperaemia failed. It shows the value, and the cause appears only in debrief problems or guided aids. For detailed IV, the pullback and thermodilution waits are based on time (Brilakis reads at 1–3 minutes), not on hyperaemia.
4. Preset titles do not name the failure. The contrast-ffr case is a 59% mid-LAD lesion: contrast FFR is about 0.824, true FFR 0.766, and the decision is treat.
5. AF and VF are kept in a separate PHYSIOLOGY_ADENOSINE_EVENTS list so that PhysiologyLab.test.ts (which expects every event in PHYSIOLOGY_PATIENT_EVENTS from an IV run) stays green.
6. The six hyperaemia presets are in PHYSIOLOGY_PRESETS so they appear in the lab's case dropdown.
7. pwSession.ts also exports IC_GTN_UG, the same 200 µg the rig uses. The legacy actions keep their compressed curves for other callers.

review.verdict:
Changes needed. The engine, pharmacology, session, panels, tips and launch file are mostly implemented to the design. The package's own tests pass: 17 + 8 + 3 new, and patient.test.ts 88/88. The typecheck (npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit) is clean. Shared engines keep their defaults: the hazard model is off unless set, the caffeine factor is exactly 1 by default, the giveDrug option is optional, pacing defaults to null, and the replay test strips only the `adn` field. No unlisted src file was changed by this package; every other file newer than .started belongs to left-main, haemo-transducer or the angio-label packages. Cited module lines check out (14-physiology.ts 98, 410, 421-422, 438, 443, 460, 478-488; 04-lab-drugs.ts 436, 505, 556, 586). The UI uses Clinical Graphite classes and British English, and shows no ground truth (the IC dose field is empty and failure causes appear only in aids or the debrief).

Four problems block acceptance:
1. The live lab rig is not wired to the new engine adapter. Until it is, the saline-swap, tissued-line, caffeine and adenosine-vf presets behave wrongly in the browser.
2. The engine judges whether an intracoronary dose is high risk from the part that reached the artery, not the dose the operator gave. A slow RCA dose between 101 and 166 µg never draws a hazard. I confirmed this with vite-node: a forced 'no-escape' stays unused after 150 µg slow, so the acceptance test that claims a forced block actually passes through the ordinary AV block draw.
3. A contrast FFR read after the contrast effect has passed is accepted as valid. At 40 s it read 0.914 with h = 0, and the debrief credited it.
4. Two assertions in physiologyTips.test.ts, a test owned by another package, now fail.

I ran: the six physiology test files (70 passed, 2 failed, both in physiologyTips.test.ts), patient.test.ts (88 passed), the typecheck, and two scratch vite-node checks saved in the scratchpad (rv/check1.ts and rv/check2.ts).

MeasurePanel now always sends detailed actions, but the rig still gives the engine its fixed doses: 200 or 100 µg IC whatever dose was entered, and a central adenosine infusion even when the session holds saline or a tissued hand line. The browser therefore shows the systemic signs of adenosine (pressure falls, heart rate rises) in saline-swap and iv-tissued-line, while the session reports no hyperaemia. This contradicts the teaching at 14-physiology.ts:460. Caffeine never reaches the engine. adenosine-vf never produces VF, because setUpPwEngine is not called. CPR, pacing, shock and cardioversion orders only write to the log. The monitor rhythm is not passed to the session, so the arrhythmia debrief items never appear. findings.fix: Land the rig patch in the same wave, either through the owning package or as an approved file-list extension. (1) In the PhysiologyRig constructor, after applyLine(), call setUpPwEngine(this.engine, this.session). (2) In dispatch(), replace `if (this.session !== before) this.applyDrug(a, before);` with `applyPwActionToEngine(this.engine, before, this.session, a);`, then delete applyDrug and the IC_ADENOSINE_UG and IC_GTN_UG duplicates, importing IC_GTN_UG from pwSession. (3) In step(), send `patient: pwPatientInput(v)` instead of `{ map, hr }`. The legacy branch of applyPwActionToEngine gives the same doses and the same side as applyDrug, so PhysiologyLab.test.ts should stay green. Then add a test to PhysiologyLab.test.ts: drive the rig on 'adenosine-vf' and expect rhythmKind 'vf' within 30 s; on 'saline-swap', run an IV infusion for 120 s and expect the mean pressure to fall by less than 3 mmHg. If the rig cannot be patched in this wave, remove the six presets from PHYSIOLOGY_PRESETS and from hyperaemia.launch.ts until it is.

findings.where: src/simulation/patient/engine.ts give() (adenosine block, about line 945) and adenosineHighRisk(); src/simulation/pci/pwSession.ts applyPwActionToEngine (the 'hyperaemia' ic and 'flush-guide' cases) and setUpPwEngine
findings.problem: The engine judges high risk on the dose it receives in each call. The session sends the bolus as two calls: 60% at the injection (1 - MP_GUIDE_HOLDUP) and 40% at the flush. A slow 150 µg RCA dose, which is above the module's 100 µg limit (14-physiology.ts:483, 04-lab-drugs.ts:556), arrives as 90 + 60 µg and is never high risk, so the real threshold becomes about 167 µg. With 'x' seeds, a forced vf fired at 170 µg slow but not at 150 µg slow. With seed 'tips', a forced no-escape was still unused after 150 µg slow. For large doses both parts can exceed 100 µg, giving two hazard draws per bolus, and the ordinary AV block draw (ADENOSINE.completeAvBlock.ic x dose/std) also runs once per part. In physiologyTips.hyperaemia.test.ts, the first test's comment says 'this run's hazard is block without an escape rhythm'. It actually passes on the ordinary block with an escape rhythm, so the forced path is never tested at session level.
findings.fix: Add `bolusUg?: number` (the whole intracoronary dose as given) and `continuation?: boolean` to InjectionDetail. In give(), for adenosine IC: if `inj?.continuation`, skip both the completeAvBlock draw and the hazard draw. Otherwise use `const whole = inj?.bolusUg ?? o.dose` in both the completeAvBlock scaling and `adenosineHighRisk(whole, ...)`. In applyPwActionToEngine and setUpPwEngine, pass `bolusUg: inj.doseUg * (inj.engaged ? 1 : MP_DISENGAGED_DELIVERY)` with the first part, and `{ continuation: true }` with the flush part. In physiologyTips.hyperaemia.test.ts, after the 150 µg slow dose and flush, assert `lab.engine.adenosineHazards()?.force === null` and that rhythmKind 'asystole' was seen (standstill). Add a pwSession.hyperaemia test checking that a slow 120 µg RCA dose plus flush calls giveDrug with bolusUg 120 and that the flush call carries continuation.

findings.problem: Any fast push counts as high risk. A low-dose fast push into a non-AV-nodal artery (for example 20 µg into the LAD) draws an arrhythmia, but the AV nodal drive never passes 0.2, so adnPending is never fired or cleared. It then fires on the next unrelated adenosine dose, possibly minutes later.

In the slow tick, set `adnPending = null` once t passes it without the drive having exceeded 0.2. Snapshot and restore the new field. Add a test: fast 20 µg into the LAD with force 'af', advance 60 s, expect pending to have gone, then give 150 µg slow into the RCA with the hazard off and expect no AF.
